query: How do I create a paper windmill?

goal.title: Make a paper pinwheel on a wooden rod
goal.description: Trim a paper square, crease both diagonals and cut four inward slits. Fold alternating corners to the center, secure them with a tiny fastener and attach the center to a thin wooden rod.
goal.final_state: A four-bladed pale paper pinwheel is attached at its center to a thin wooden rod and laid on the table. The video does not establish free rotation under airflow.

procedure.description: Hold the pale paper sheet in the left hand and use scissors in the right to trim a narrow strip and remaining edge, producing a square. Put the scissors beside the sheet and lay the square on the table.
Bring opposite corners together diagonally to form a triangle. Smooth the fold, lift its edge and pinch along the crease, then unfold the square.
Bring the other pair of corners together, align the layers and crease the second diagonal by pressing and pinching it. Open the sheet again, revealing crossing diagonal creases.

Pick up the scissors, cut from one corner along a diagonal toward but short of the center, rotate the sheet and repeat at the remaining three corners. Leave an uncut central area and put the scissors down.
Lay the slit square flat. Bring one cut corner inward and press it, rotate the paper as needed and repeat with alternating corners, gathering four tips at the center to make four angled blades.

Lift and steady the gathered blades, retrieve a tiny fastener from the table and push it through or into the overlapping center with the right fingers. Its exact type and connection are too small to resolve.

Retrieve a thin wooden rod, align its tip behind the pinwheel center and work the central fastener while holding the paper and rod together. Turn the assembly forward and adjust the center until the four blades remain gathered on the rod.
Hold and turn the assembled paper pinwheel by its rod, inspect the center and blades, then lay it on the table. A free spin under wind is not demonstrated.

coarse.instruction: Trim the paper into a square
coarse.description: Hold the paper while cutting away an edge strip and trimming the remaining side. Put the scissors down and arrange the square on the table.
coarse.goal_contribution: Produces the square blank for the pinwheel.

coarse.description: Fold opposite corners together, align and press the first diagonal, unfold, then repeat with the other pair of corners. Open the sheet to reveal crossed creases.
coarse.goal_contribution: Marks the center and cutting directions while keeping one sheet intact.
coarse.predictability_reason: The square paper needs diagonal creases for the pinwheel shape.

coarse.description: Retrieve scissors and cut inward from each corner along its diagonal, rotating the sheet between cuts and stopping before the central intersection. Put the scissors down.
coarse.goal_contribution: Separates the corner sections that can be folded into blades.
coarse.predictability_reason: Creased diagonals guide the corner slits.

coarse.description: Bring alternating cut corners into the center one after another, press each tip and rotate the paper between corners.
coarse.goal_contribution: Forms four angled blades whose tips meet at the center.
coarse.predictability_reason: Cut corner slits are ready to fold into blades.

coarse.instruction: Secure the blades and attach the rod
coarse.description: Retrieve and work a tiny center fastener through the gathered tips, pick up a wooden rod and attach the center to its end. Turn and adjust the assembly, then hold and lay down the finished pinwheel.
coarse.goal_contribution: Keeps the folded blades together and provides a handle for the paper pinwheel.
coarse.predictability_reason: Gathered blades need fastening and a rod.
